# google-classroom-student-mcp

> Free, open source, read only Google Classroom MCP server that lets AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and others) read a student's Google Classroom courses, assignments, due dates, missing work, grades, announcements and a catch up digest. It cannot submit, edit or delete anything.

## Setup
- Needs GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN.
- Optional: set CLASSROOM_TIMEZONE, for example America/Toronto. Work with a due date but no due time is due at the end of that day in that zone. The default is the zone of the computer running the server.
- Run the one time login command from the README to get a refresh token.
- Run `npx google-classroom-student-mcp setup` to print a ready to paste mcpServers block for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP apps.
- Run with npx -y google-classroom-student-mcp. Run `npx google-classroom-student-mcp doctor` to check the setup.

## Tools (all read only)
- get_my_courses: List the student's active Google Classroom classes with their IDs. Use this when the user asks 'What classes am I in?' or needs a course ID to pass to another tool.
- get_todo: Everything assigned that the student has not turned in yet, each with a link to open it in Classroom. Pass course_ids to limit it, or leave empty for all active classes. Use this when the user asks 'What do I still have to do?' or 'What's left to turn in across all my classes?'
- export_due_dates_calendar: Build an ICS calendar file of upcoming due dates so they can be imported into a calendar app. Pass course_ids to limit it, or leave empty for all active classes. Use this when the user asks 'Can you give me my due dates as a calendar file?'
- get_upcoming_due_dates: Work that is due soon and not turned in, soonest first. Pass course_ids or days_ahead to narrow it, or leave both empty. Use this when the user asks 'What's due this week across all my classes?' or 'What's coming up?'
- get_missing_assignments: Past due work that has not been turned in. Pass course_ids to limit it, or leave empty for all active classes. Use this when the user asks 'What's overdue?' or 'What am I behind on?'
- get_assignments: Assignments for one class with due dates and status, each with a link to open it in Classroom. Use this when the user asks 'What's due in this class?' or wants every assignment and its points for a single class.
- get_assignment_details: Everything about one assignment: what the teacher wrote in the description, the files and links attached to it, its due date, points and your status. Pass the course ID and the assignment ID. Use this when the user asks 'What does this assignment ask for?' or 'What do I need to turn in?' about one specific assignment.
- get_my_grades: Grades on returned work for each class, with the comment the teacher left on the work. Google Classroom has no overall grade, so this adds up graded work only, and adds a weighted percent when the class uses grading categories with weights. Pass course_ids to limit it, or leave empty for all active classes. Use this when the user asks 'How am I doing in my classes?' or 'What grades have I gotten back?'
- get_target_grade: Points needed on the work that is left to reach a target percent in each class. Adds up the points earned on graded work and the points the work left is worth, then says how many of those points you still need. target_percent is the percent you want, from 0 to 100. Pass course_ids to limit it, or leave empty for all active classes. Use this when the user asks 'What do I need to score to get a 90?' or 'Can I still get an A in this class?'
- get_announcements: Recent announcements, each with a link to open it in Classroom. Pass course_ids or since_days to limit how far back they go, or leave empty for all active classes. Use this when the user asks 'Did my teacher post anything new?' or 'What did my teacher announce?'
- get_course_materials: Posted materials for one class, grouped by topic with the Drive link of every attached file. Use this when the user asks 'What materials did my teacher post?' or 'What did we cover in unit 3?' or wants the readings, slides and handouts for one class.
- get_whats_new: One catch up digest for every class: new announcements, newly graded work with the comment the teacher left, overdue work and what is due next. Pass course_ids to limit it, since_days for how far back to look and days_ahead for how far ahead to look. Use this when the user asks 'What's new since yesterday?' or 'What changed in my classes?'

get_todo, export_due_dates_calendar, get_upcoming_due_dates, get_missing_assignments, get_my_grades, get_target_grade and get_whats_new take an optional course_ids list to check specific classes only. get_upcoming_due_dates and get_whats_new also take an optional days_ahead number. get_announcements and get_whats_new also take an optional since_days number for how far back to look; it defaults to 7 days in the digest and means no date filter in announcements. get_announcements takes optional course_ids too. get_target_grade takes a required target_percent from 0 to 100, which is the class percent you want.

get_todo, get_assignments, get_announcements and get_course_materials print the Classroom page of each item under the title, so the AI can hand the student a direct link to the work. get_course_materials also prints the Drive link of every file attached to a material. Classroom sends a link only for published items.

get_my_grades and get_whats_new print what the teacher wrote when they returned the work, under the score, with the Classroom page of the work. get_my_grades lists the graded work that has a comment under each class.

get_target_grade adds up the points earned on graded work and the points the work that is left is worth. It then works out how many of those points you need to reach target_percent. Work counts as left when it has points and no grade yet, and work the teacher already returned without a grade is left out. If the target needs more points than the work left is worth, the answer says so and gives the best percent you can still reach. The server only sees the points on each piece of work, not any weighting the teacher may use, so the answer counts every point the same.

An announcement counts as new when it was posted or changed inside the window. The date of a new grade comes from the teacher's comment on the work when there is one, otherwise from the last change to the assignment. The comment itself is printed under the grade.

## Questions students ask
- "What do I still need to turn in?" goes to get_todo: every assignment you have not handed in, with a link to open it in Classroom.
- "What does this assignment ask for?" goes to get_assignment_details: the teacher's description, the files and links attached to the assignment, its due date, points and your status.
- "Can you give me my due dates as a calendar file?" goes to export_due_dates_calendar: build an ICS calendar file of upcoming due dates.
- "What's overdue?" goes to get_missing_assignments: work that was due and is still not handed in.
- "What's due this week across all my classes?" goes to get_upcoming_due_dates: work that is due soon, soonest first.
- "What did my teacher say about my work?" goes to get_my_grades: the comment the teacher left on the graded work, with the score and a link to open it in Classroom.
- "What do I need to score to get a 90?" goes to get_target_grade: the points you need on the work that is left to reach that percent in each class.
- "What did my teachers post lately?" goes to get_announcements: recent announcements from every class.
- "What's new since yesterday?" goes to get_whats_new: new announcements, new grades, overdue work and what is due next.

## Example answer
The question "What's due this week across all my classes?" is answered by get_upcoming_due_dates, which prints one line per assignment, soonest first:
```text
- Essay outline (English) due Fri, Oct 23
- Lab write up (Biology) due Fri, Oct 23, 11:59 p.m. UTC
- Problem set 4 (Calculus) due Mon, Oct 26
```

Every line has the assignment title, the class and the due date. Work you already turned in is left out. Classroom keeps due times in UTC, and the server prints them in your own time zone.

### Example answer for get_todo
The question "What do I still need to turn in?" is answered by get_todo, which prints everything you have not handed in and puts the Classroom page of each one under the title:
```text
- Lab safety form (English) due Fri, Oct 9
  link: https://classroom.google.com/c/English/course/1/courseWork/w2
- Chapter 3 questions (Biology) due Mon, Oct 19
  link: https://classroom.google.com/c/Biology/course/2/courseWork/w4
- Essay outline (English) due Fri, Oct 23
  link: https://classroom.google.com/c/English/course/1/courseWork/w1
- Lab write up (Biology) due Fri, Oct 23, 11:59 p.m. UTC
  link: https://classroom.google.com/c/Biology/course/2/courseWork/w3
- Problem set 4 (Calculus) due Mon, Oct 26
  link: https://classroom.google.com/c/Calculus/course/3/courseWork/w5
```

Work you already turned in is left out, and work with no due date goes last.

### Example answer for get_missing_assignments
The question "What's overdue?" is answered by get_missing_assignments, which prints the work that was due and is still not handed in, the most recent due date first:
```text
- Chapter 3 questions (Biology) was due Mon, Oct 19
- Lab safety form (English) was due Fri, Oct 9
```

### Example answer for get_whats_new
The question "What's new since yesterday?" is answered by get_whats_new, which prints one digest with new announcements, new grades, overdue work and what is due next. The times in this sample are in UTC.
```text
New announcements (last 7 days)
- Biology (Wed, Oct 21, 8:00 a.m. UTC) Field trip permission slip due Friday
- English (Tue, Oct 20, 9:00 a.m. UTC) Bring your textbook

New grades (last 7 days)
- Midterm review (Calculus) graded 88/100 on Tue, Oct 20, 3:00 p.m. UTC
  teacher said: Good work on the analysis. Watch the units on question 3.
  link: https://classroom.google.com/c/Calculus/course/3/courseWork/w6

Overdue work
- Chapter 3 questions (Biology) was due Mon, Oct 19
- Lab safety form (English) was due Fri, Oct 9

Due next (14 days)
- Essay outline (English) due Fri, Oct 23
- Lab write up (Biology) due Fri, Oct 23, 11:59 p.m. UTC
- Problem set 4 (Calculus) due Mon, Oct 26
```
